name: eBay

summary.text: eBay Inc. is an online marketplace company. It announced on July 8, 2002 an agreement (dated July 7) to acquire PayPal, Inc. in a tax-free stock-for-stock deal at a fixed ratio of 0.39 eBay shares per PayPal share, valued at about $1.5 billion on eBay's July 5 closing price. PayPal shareholders approved the merger on October 3, 2002 and it closed that day, making PayPal a wholly owned eBay subsidiary; Peter Thiel resigned as PayPal's CEO the same day. Biographies and reference works report that Elon Musk, PayPal's largest shareholder, received about $176 million in the deal and Thiel about $55 million; these figures are not from filings.

facts.claim: eBay announced on July 8, 2002 that it had agreed to acquire PayPal, Inc. in a tax-free, stock-for-stock transaction at a fixed exchange ratio of 0.39 of an eBay share for each PayPal share, valued at about $1.5 billion using eBay's July 5, 2002 closing price, with estimated acquisition-related costs of $18 million; the merger agreement was dated July 7, 2002 and closing was expected around year-end 2002.
facts.quote: eBay Inc. (Nasdaq: EBAY) today announced that it has agreed to acquire PayPal, Inc. (Nasdaq: PYPL), the global payments platform.

sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (PayPal Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)
sources.title: eBay and PayPal joint press release announcing merger agreement

facts.claim: PayPal shareholders approved the merger on October 3, 2002 and eBay completed the acquisition later that day, making PayPal a wholly owned subsidiary; eBay's completion release valued the deal using eBay's average closing price from two days before to two days after the announcement and put acquisition costs at about $17 million. Peter Thiel resigned as PayPal's CEO on completion and Matt Bannick took over his responsibilities.
facts.quote: Shareholders of PayPal approved the merger that day, and the merger was completed later that day, making PayPal a wholly owned eBay subsidiary.

facts.claim: Reported proceeds from the eBay deal: Elon Musk, PayPal's largest shareholder (11.7% before the June 2002 secondary offering), is reported to have received about $176 million, a figure that comes from Ashlee Vance's biography; Peter Thiel is reported to have made about $55 million. These figures are from biographies and reference works, not from a filing; eBay's Form S-4 and S-4/A for the merger give the 0.39 exchange ratio and the holders' share counts, and the value realised depended on eBay's share price and when shares were sold.
facts.quote: reportedly made $55 million from the total $1.5 billion sale

openQuestions: The brief says the deal netted 'the Musk syndicate over $175M+' and 'the Thiel network hundreds of millions'. The sourced figures are about $176 million for Musk personally (Vance via Wikipedia; consistent with the brief) and about $55 million for Thiel personally (EBSCO). No source retrieved supports 'hundreds of millions' for Thiel or a defined 'Thiel network'; eBay's S-4 says PayPal insiders and investors holding about 28.1% signed the July 7, 2002 voting agreement (recorded in elon-musk.json), but no source aggregates their proceeds.

The eBay S-4/A beneficial-ownership table (share counts for Thiel, Musk and other holders at the record date) was in the search results but its content was not returned; the search budget ran out before a targeted query could run. It would give filing-based share counts to multiply by the exchange ratio.
Whether Musk or Thiel sold eBay shares immediately after closing, and at what price, is not established; the $176 million and $55 million figures are value estimates, not realised cash.
